observations: Three photos show multiple electronic keyboards wrapped in clear plastic, standing upright on a tiled floor.
The keyboards have white and black keys, with some having a blue or purple panel on the left side.
The keyboards appear to be of similar design, with a small display screen and control buttons on the right side.
The plastic wrapping is crinkled and shows signs of handling, suggesting they are new or recently unpacked.
No brand or model name is visible on any of the keyboards in any photo.
The background includes a wall with a fan and some boxes, possibly in a shop or storage area.
The watermark 'MARY OLUGBAMI POSTED ON JIJI' is present on all photos.

claims.evidence: The photos show multiple keyboards, but no visible brand or model to confirm quality or price. The term 'quality' is subjective and cannot be verified remotely.

risks.risk: The keyboards may be damaged or non-functional despite being wrapped in plastic.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the keyboard's display screen and control buttons, showing no cracks or damage, and a video of the keyboard being powered on and playing a note.

risks.risk: The keyboards may be counterfeit or low-quality knockoffs, not genuine brands.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the brand name and model number on the keyboard, preferably on the back or underside.

risks.risk: The keyboards may be missing accessories such as power adapters, cables, or manuals.
risks.proof: A photo showing all included accessories laid out next to the keyboard.

proof_requests: A clear photo of the brand and model name on the keyboard, preferably on the back or underside.
A close-up photo of the display screen and control buttons to check for damage.
A video of the keyboard being powered on and playing a note.
A photo showing all included accessories (power adapter, cables, manual, etc.).
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
